text: As I mentioned in my Budget cut last year, "The Government is providing funds to help firms scale-up and internationalise and helping build capabilities to operate overseas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should do the same for our IPCs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should support our local IPCs who internationalise, who fly the Singapore flag proudly overseas and who lend a helping hand to our neighbours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us not be seen to just venture into other countries to compete, to take but also to give and to help." Many of these charities and IPCs depend on volunteers and donations from private fundraising activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There may be a dampening effect on fundraising for these charities, often already faced with additional barriers to fundraising, such as the 80:20 rule.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These charities promote the Singapore spirit of generosity in some of the most difficult places, and should receive our fullest support.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also raise the issue of crowdfunding, which has proven to be an effective platform for the needy, but have also suffered a few cases of malpractice.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the Commissioner will be issuing a new code of practice for crowdfunding, but I would like to ask the reason for not including these changes into the Charity Act and thus making them mandatory.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This suggests that there is room for the majority of charities in Singapore to enhance their performance in the criteria assessed, such as financial management, internal control, fundraising management and conflict of interest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I suspect that this is because most charities are resource-strapped.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just like ACRES, we often rely on volunteers, a very small pool of full-time staff members and limited funding, and are often busy fighting day-to-day fires.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have read the Ministry's response to feedback received through REACH and have found it to be very comprehensive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It also showed that feedback received from the public was well-researched and proved to be constructive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that more Bills will undergo similar public engagement, something that I firmly believe will help us to draft the best Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I stand in support of the Bill, and I am sorry, Sir, I forgot to declare at the onset.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I declare my interest as the Chief Executive of a charity.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I welcome the amendments to strengthen Government oversight and raise governance standards of the charities sector.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If our charities sector is to grow, we must ensure that donations are utilised as intended and reach their targeted clients.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These accounts should, of course, be publicly available for scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Besides meeting submission criteria and standards required by auditors of the COC, these numbers should be accompanied by brief notes in simple English so that donors and interested parties can have a clear idea of how the funds are used.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The directors' and key management's fees, as well as all related party transactions, if any, must be laid out to ensure arms' length transactions.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I do not think such requirements are too onerous nor tedious.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Good housekeeping and the provision of regular updates are key to sustainability and a small price to pay towards gaining the trust of donors in a charity.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A good growing reputation will attract even more funds to support its cause.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such controls will help reduce incidences of where disproportionate amounts of money are used to pay for commissions, salaries, fees and purposes other than direct assistance for the intended beneficiaries and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, the amendments seek to clarify the definition of a fundraising appeal to ensure that all such appeals are subject to regulatory requirements.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I feel that we can do more to address the proliferation of online fundraisers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In particular, how does the Government intend to monitor and ensure compliance from entities not based in Singapore, even as they reach out to Singaporeans and residents for funds?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I conclude my support for the Bill.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members have raised several points on the scope of the regulation of fundraising appeals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan have made certain enquiries about the scope of fundraising appeals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All fundraising appeals, whether online or offline, whether for local or foreign purposes, have been and continue to be subject to the Act.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Act also imposes obligations on persons and organisations raising funds or receiving the funds raised.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A person raising funds via an online fundraising platform for a needy family will contravene the law if the funds raised are not applied to the said cause.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A charity that is in the service of providing nursing care for the elderly has an obligation under the law to ensure that any unsolicited donation it receives is applied to the said object.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Therefore, the examples that Mr Louis Ng and also the point raised by Mr Dennis Tan about small-scale private fundraising activities and unsolicited donations are therefore bound by the Act.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: However, we are mindful not to stifle giving while safeguarding public interest.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We recognise that fundraising appeals come in a wide range of scale and complexity, from bake sales to nationwide campaigns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As explained in my earlier speech, we regulate fundraising activities through the Charities (Fundraising Appeals for Local and Foreign Charitable Purposes) Regulations 2012 in a risk-adjusted approach.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In practice, we have exempted all appeals for local causes from the requirement to apply for permits.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This exemption has also been extended to appeals for donations-in-kind for foreign causes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will review the administrative requirements on fundraising, including for foreign causes, an issue that was raised by Mr Ng.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This framework of scoping the regulatory requirements through the regulations allow us to be nimble and responsive to the needs of the sector and the public.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Louis Ng referred to the 80:20 rule as a barrier to fundraising for foreign causes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The 80:20 rule stipulates that with regard to fundraising for foreign charitable purposes, at least 80% of funds collected by the fundraiser must go towards charitable purposes in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This ensures that resources are not collected from the public for overseas causes at the expense of local needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I will also like to point out that the Commissioner can and does, on a case-by-case basis, waive this rule to support, for example, appeals in aid of providing immediate humanitarian and disaster relief.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many Members, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Louis Ng, Ms Denise Phua, Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Joan Pereira and Ms Thanaletchimi, have spoken on the proliferation of online fundraising appeals and asked how we regulate these appeals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Allow me to explain that the Act is not of extraterritorial application.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If the appeal is conducted by an individual residing overseas and it is not targeted at residents in Singapore, the appeal may not be deemed to be carried out in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Such appeals are not regulated by the Commissioner as we do not have extraterritorial jurisdiction.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Where a fundraising appeal falls under our purview, the Commissioner will investigate if contravention of our regulations is suspected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This includes investigating cases of alleged misrepresentation or half-truths that Members spoke about.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members of the public should report suspicious fundraising appeals to the Commissioner.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Where irregularities are found, the Commissioner can stop the appeal and direct a fund raiser to refund donations collected, a point that Mr Melvin Yong has asked.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members have called for greater regulation in the online sphere.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We recognise that online platforms bring convenience to donors and have the potential to expand the reach and impact of fundraising campaigns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Given the ease of conducting online fundraising appeals and the speed with which funds are raised, the online channels are proliferating.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Coupled with the anonymity of the Internet, regulating the online fundraising sector is a complex and difficult task.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our approach is one of co-regulation, where a safe online giving environment is a shared responsibility.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are collaborating with the sector, specifically the crowdfunding intermediaries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will create greater awareness and nudge both intermediaries and fundraisers in the online sphere towards complying with the Code of Practice.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The best practices in the Code include conducting due diligence to ensure the legitimacy of appeals, providing up-to-date information on funds raised and fees charged, and maintaining proper records of donations received and disbursed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Under the Code, crowdfunding platforms will require fundraisers to declare their awareness and compliance with key regulatory requirements when using their platforms.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This serves to remind fundraisers of their duties and obligations of providing information that is complete and true, and ensure that funds raised are used only for the declared objectives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Commissioner will publish the list of compliant platforms and encourage the public to donate through these intermediaries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: While we put in place regulations and guidelines on the fundraisers, donors have a part to play in practising safe giving, both in the online and offline spheres.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are stepping up public education efforts to empower the public with the knowledge and skills to better differentiate legitimate appeals from those that are not.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will customise our safe giving guidance for different segments of the population to ensure effective communication.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This could range from hardcopy infographics for the elderly, to posts and references on social media.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members have raised several suggestions on enhancing governance, transparency and accountability of charities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We agree that these attributes are key to gaining the trust of donors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: However, we are mindful of the compliance costs that are imposed on charities, a point that Ms Denise Phua has raised.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are therefore constantly weighing the benefits and costs of regulations to be imposed and seeking to strike the right balance, the right balance that she has talked about.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The majority of our charities conduct their activities responsibly.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we agree totally with Ms Chia's point.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Given the profile of our charities, we have assessed that an annual reporting requirement is adequate for the sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is in response to Mr Gan's point.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Charities are required to submit an annual report containing a review of their activities as well as their financial statements, which are published for public access.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For IPCs and larger charities, they are subject to more stringent requirements, such as audits by a public accountant and disclosure requirements in line with accounting standards.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This includes disclosures in the charity's financial statements on related party transactions, as well as explanatory notes on the use of funds.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If there is a reason, such as in the case of a charity being investigated, the Commissioner will require more frequent updates on its activities and financials.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would like now to clarify on certain points raised by Members on the reporting requirements for registered charities and exempt charities, a point that Ms Chia Yong Yong has raised.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As part of the review, the Commissioner also took the opportunity to clarify the regulatory requirements that would apply to registered charities and exempt charities which enjoy tax benefits.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In response to Ms Chia, we do have charities which are not successful in their application for registration as they do not meet certain requirements, such as having a purpose that is substantially beneficial to the community in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, there are certain reporting requirements that do not apply to these charities that have not been successful in registration.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In addition to regulatory requirements, the Code of Governance for Charities and IPCs applies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Code of Governance serves as a best practices guide in key areas of governance and management, and comprises tiered guidelines depending on the status and size of the charity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To accommodate the diversity in governance structures across charities, we believe that the current "Comply or Explain" principle is relevant.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Charities' reasons for non-compliance with the Code will be published.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Commissioner takes into account the reasons for non-compliance with the Code in assessing a charity's application for IPC status and in selecting charities for review.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The board members of a charity have a fiduciary duty to ensure that the charity is governed and managed responsibly by ensuring that funds are used prudently and in accordance with the intended purposes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Nevertheless, we agree with the Members that more can be done so that stakeholders have greater clarity on how a charity's funds are used.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Commissioner will be developing a guide to help all charities, big and small, put out key information, both financial and non-financial, in a manner that will help donors and other stakeholders understand the financial position, use of donations and activities of a charity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Several Members have raised points on the powers and provisions relating to the protection of charities, donors and charitable assets.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, Mr Melvin Yong, Ms Joan Pereira, Ms Thanaletchimi, Mr Alex Yam and Ms Denise Phua have raised some points.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In proposing amendments to the Act, due consideration is given to ensure that the powers given to the Commissioner are fair, reasonable and essential, with sufficient safeguards in place.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Bill proposes to allow the Commissioner to extend the suspension of persons from their positions in a charity and suspend improper fundraising appeals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Chia has asked whether such suspensions should be extended to 24 months in the first instance, while Mr Yong is concerned with the potential disruption to the charity during the suspension.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have assessed the proposed increase from 12 to 24 months to be fair and reasonable.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It should be noted that when the Commissioner orders a charity to suspend an improper fundraising appeal, the suspension does not prohibit the charity from conducting other fundraising appeals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, for example, if the fundraising appeal in question is for the building of a new facility, the charity can continue to raise funds for its operations while the questionable appeal is being suspended.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During any period of suspension, as with any serious situation requiring the Commissioner's intervention, the Commissioner will work closely with the governing board of the charity to ensure the continuity of its operations and services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We may review the necessity to extend the suspension period further later.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Thanaletchimi asked if the risk is real.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which is an intergovernmental standard-setting body for combating money laundering and terrorism financing has, in recent years, noted the increasing role of non-profit organisations in terrorism financing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The risk is, therefore, real and increasing, and that is the reason for us to strengthen our legislation in this regard.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And I will take note of Ms Thanaletchimi's advice for us not to stress that this only relates to charities with an object in religion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Alex Yam queried about the number of money laundering or terrorism financing cases that the Commissioner has investigated.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It would only take one case of a charity in Singapore being involved in money laundering or terrorism financing to shake public confidence in the charity sector as well as in the wider sector, including the financial sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The proposed amendment, therefore, seeks to strengthen our regulatory regime in light of emerging risks and signals our commitment to ensure that charities are not misused to provide a front for such unlawful activities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Member has also asked about the permanence of disqualifications where spent convictions are involved.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As mentioned in my earlier speech, where a person is disqualified under the Act on the ground of a criminal conviction, such as for an offence involving dishonesty, the disqualification ceases once the conviction becomes spent, or the person receives a pardon for the offence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Removals under the Act, on the other hand, are permanent.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If a person is removed on the ground of a criminal conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude, he will be permanently barred from returning to that charity as a board member or key officer.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The permanence is intended as the cause for removal is serious in respect of the charity that he is serving, and it is a result of deliberate consideration.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the case of removal after inquiry for mismanagement or misconduct, the removed person is barred from key positions in the rest of the sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the protection of charities' governing board members, as raised by Ms Denise Phua, we acknowledge the responsibility placed on the governing board members of our charities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As trustees of public funds, they must act with reasonable care and skill to lead charities to do good work well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The law protects those who have acted honestly and reasonably from personal liability.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And in response to Mr Dennis Tan's point earlier about the difference between board members and key officers, these are two separate groups of persons, as mentioned in the Act.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Key officers would be officers in the company or in the charity that have influence on key decisions and are involved in the control of management and operations of the company.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some board members could also be assuming key officer roles, but they are two separate categories altogether.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it does not mean that a key officer who is not a board member will be relieved of his obligations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A key officer will be restricted, as we defined it, to a few persons who have management control of the outfit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, typically, in a very small charity, that probably would relate to the General Manager or the Chief Executive Officer.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We echo Members' call for greater support for charities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First, on capability building, we are working closely with the Centre for Non-profit Leadership to reach out to professionals with the heart to serve and pair them up with charities who need help.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong and Ms Denise Phua have made a very strong and convincing case about the need for the sector to attract talent and to professionalise the sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Commissioner will work with partners, including professional bodies, to engage charities and share know-how.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Townhall sessions and the annual Charity Governance Conference are some examples of capability building efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Second, on processes, the Commissioner is looking at simplifying regulatory reporting, with a focus on effective reporting.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will be particularly helpful to smaller charities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Third, on cost, the Commissioner is working with partners, such as the apex organisations, to set up shared services that charities can tap on.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong has called for collaboration.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These shared services may explore the suggestions brought up by these Members to assist charities which are experiencing either temporary problems or to help strengthen their compliance, governance and effectiveness.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To assist these charities, we provide support via the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund for the purchase of computers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They may also tap on the shared services facilities mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Next, working with our stakeholders and customising our regulatory approach.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Denise Phua made a wonderful speech calling for greater customisation of our regulatory approach.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We recognise that the charity sector is diverse and reaches out to different parts of the society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To this end, the Commissioner works closely with different stakeholders to achieve our shared vision.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They serve as points of contact for the charities in their sector and work closely with the Commissioner to ensure consistency in the regulatory stance and effective regulation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many of our capability building initiatives are also tailored based on the needs of the respective sectors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For instance, following the launch of the refined Code of Governance in April 2017, we worked with different partners, including apex organisations for different sectors, to conduct sharing sessions on the Code for their respective sectors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to assess how to better customise in our future reviews.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will take them into consideration for the next round of the review.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As fellow Members have rightly expressed, trust is key for the charity sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The underlying objective of our proposed legislative amendments is to enhance this trust.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In proposing the amendments, we have also held fast to our commitment of a balanced regulatory framework.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to have a charity sector that not only has the trust and confidence of the public, but also one that is healthy and thriving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is our goal to nurture a charity sector that remains driven by the community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to encourage co-regulation and a culture of transparency, and our regulatory approach will reflect this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to work with partners, such as the Charity Council and professional bodies, to help charities strengthen their capabilities and governance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are encouraged by the vision that leaders of the sector, such as Ms Chia Yong Yong and Ms Denise Phua, have painted for us and we are committed to supporting such ground-up initiatives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will step up public education efforts to empower donors to give wisely and to donate with both the head and heart.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Charities, too, need to ensure that they are well-governed and accountable to win the trust of the public, especially their donors and volunteers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Together, our efforts will help the charity sector flourish.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A healthy and vibrant charity sector is the bedrock to a caring and cohesive Singapore.
